summary.tagline: Saltstraumen (Norwegian) or Stuorstrávve (Lule Sami) is a small strait with one of the strongest tidal current

days.title: Fjords and Small Currents
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM start, after checking official access hours

stops.name: Saltfjord
stops.detail: Through a 2.5 kilometer long and about 150 meter wide sound, almost 400 million cubic meters of water flow back and forth between the Saltfjord at the sea and the Skjerstadfjord inland (also called "Inner Saltfjord") as the tides change.

stops.name: Skjerstadfjord
stops.detail: Due to tidal choking, the tidal range in the Skjerstadfjord is lower compared to the Saltfjord and is delayed by 1 hour and 41 minutes, as is the time of the tide reversal.

stops.name: Godøystraumen
stops.detail: The water flow through the Godøystraumen between Knaplundsøya and the mainland is even smaller.

stops.name: Brücke
stops.detail: The coastal road Fv17 leads over the current on a bridge and offers impressive views.

stops.name: Ufer des Saltstraumen
stops.detail: The banks of the Saltstraumen offer popular fishing spots, as the nutrient-rich water attracts fish.

stops.name: Saltstraumen Museum
stops.detail: In the summer season, the Saltstraumen Museum, Ripnesveien, provides information on local and natural history on Wednesdays and weekends.

stops.name: Kongebautaen
stops.detail: A ten-minute walk away to the northwest, the Kongebautaen monument commemorates the visits of three majesties.
